title: Artificial Intelligence guided 3D-Reconstruction for Lung Surgery
summary:
With modern imaging techniques such as computed tomography (CT), lung cancer is now often detected at a very early stage. In many cases, instead of removing an entire lobe of the lung as in the past, a smaller operation is sufficient, in which only a part of the lung – called a segment – is removed. This segmentectomy preserves more healthy lung tissue but is technically more demanding, especially in minimally invasive surgery where the tumor cannot be palpated.

Additionally, the blood vessels and bronchi in the lungs vary from person to person, which can further complicate the procedure.

This is where the new technology comes in: Using artificial intelligence, a precise 3D model of the lung is created from the CT images. This model shows the tumor, the exact course of the vessels and bronchi, and the location of the lung segments. This may allow for better surgical planning and safer execution of the procedure.

This study investigates whether this technique makes the surgery safer and allows for even more precise tumor removal. Two groups will be compared:

One group will undergo surgery using the new 3D technology.

The other group will undergo surgery following the standard procedure without a 3D model.

The study will record, among other things, the duration of the operation, the amount of blood loss, the length of hospital stay, and whether any complications occur. It will also assess whether the tumor has been completely removed and monitor the disease course in the years following the surgery.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung

interventions.name:
Patients with AI-assisted 3D reconstruction

An individual, AI-based 3D model of the pulmonary anatomy is generated from preoperative CT data (using software from Infervision).

The 3D model is used for surgical planning and intraoperative guidance.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients capable of giving informed consent, aged >18 years, suspected malignant lung tumor, Tumor location: central and adjacent to vascular structures, High-resolution CT scan with a slice thickness of at least 2 mm
Exclusion criteria:
No informed consent provided by the patient, Age < 18 years
